value.title: Write a procedure
value.summary: How to write a procedure: look first, book the id, write it from what really happens with recipes that check their own preconditions, pass the drift check, then get the operator's yes.

value.who: Any seat doing repeatable work that no procedure covers yet; the operator approves it.
value.when: Before repeatable work with no procedure, or while doing it the first time (rule 0: find the procedure and follow it, or write it as you go).

value.name: area
value.description: the procedure's area (lowercase letters and digits)
value.fallback: pick the area of the role that will own it: daemon, fleet, build, release in pij; meta and docs only in the skill

value.name: slug
value.description: a few kebab-case words naming the job

value.name: title
value.description: the title, as an instruction ("Bounce the daemon after an rs merge")

value.title: Look for a procedure that already covers the job
value.done_when: You know no procedure covers it. If one does, follow that one instead and fix it if it is wrong.

value.title: Book the id and create the folder
value.done_when: The folder exists with a valid procedure document (and a justfile for a runnable one), staged in your feature worktree.

value.title: Write it from what really happens
value.done_when: Every placeholder is replaced: steps are recipes with preconditions and done checks, inputs say their fallback, links carry a sentence.

value.title: Get the operator's yes
value.done_when: The operator said yes and `proc status current <id> --approved-by <operator>` recorded it. Until then the draft is usable as it is.

sections.name: done_when
sections.value: A procedure exists for the job, it passes the drift check, and the operator's approval (or its absence) is on record.

value.text: `who` on a step is stated and printed, not enforced (PRD 005 q-05).
The runner reads preconditions as recipes; there is no predicate language (PRD 005 n-1).
Writing a precondition only in prose or in "common mistakes". If a step can fail because something isn't ready, make it a `pre` check that refuses with its fix.
Booking in the main checkout or on main: `new` refuses; make a feature worktree first.
Copying a shared script into the folder. Only what this procedure alone uses lives here; shared tooling is listed in `uses`.

value.guarantees: This is the procedure req-23 asks for: how to write a procedure, with the survey's pitfalls, the two rules and the drafting pattern.
Step 0001 is rule 0: look for the procedure before doing repeatable work.
